details: Bitcoin dropped below $63,000, influenced by several factors, including three Federal Reserve board members reportedly voting for an interest rate hike at Wednesday's meeting. Adding to the downward pressure were disappointing second-quarter earnings from major crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which saw its stock tumble over 10%. Persistent doubts about the passage of the Clarity Act—a crucial piece of US crypto legislation—before the August recess further dampened market sentiment. The overall risk-off environment, coupled with institutional selling pressure from spot Bitcoin ETFs and corporate treasuries, contributed to the cryptocurrency's decline.
title: Bitcoin Slides Amid Fed Rate Hike Speculation and Coinbase Earnings Miss

details: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh maintained a firm stance on bringing inflation down to the 2% target, yet the central bank opted to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting on Wednesday (July 29, 2026). This "hawkish hold," coupled with Warsh's hints at potentially changing the Fed's inflation measurement strategy, created uncertainty among investors. The lack of clear forward guidance on rate policy led to a sharp selloff in bonds, pushing 30-year Treasury yields above 5.2%—a 19-year high. This environment generally reduces investor appetite for risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Fed's "Hawkish Hold" on Rates Fuels Inflation Concerns and Higher Treasury Yields

details: On July 31, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) released the accessibility standards for its forthcoming digital euro application, aiming for a system that exceeds European accessibility law requirements. The ECB has already selected 36 payment service providers to participate in a 12-month pilot program set to commence in the second half of 2027. This initiative, designed to complement physical cash by offering a public digital payment option, has a potential issuance target of 2029. The digital euro is expected to introduce significant competition for existing stablecoins and private payment tokens within the European market.
title: ECB Unveils Digital Euro Accessibility Standards, Pilot Nears

details: A recent report indicates that Wall Street firms and professional investors now dominate crypto trading, accounting for approximately 72% of spot trading volume on major market maker Wintermute's over-the-counter desk in the first half of 2026. This shift towards institutional participation has led to a significant decrease in realized volatility, from around 70% in earlier market cycles to about 45% currently. Institutional investors tend to hold positions longer and operate within defined risk limits, contributing to a calmer, more mature market. Additionally, tokenized real-world assets, particularly Treasuries and private credit, are gaining traction, with BNY Mellon launching Digital Transfer Agency capabilities to support both digital and traditional asset funds.
title: Wall Street Drives Crypto Trading, Lowering Volatility

details: Binance.US plans to apply to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) next month (August 2026) for a designated contract market license. This move is part of the exchange's strategy to introduce regulated futures, options, and event contracts for retail customers in the US, aiming to diversify revenue streams and reclaim market share after previous regulatory challenges.
title: Binance.US to Pursue Prediction Markets License

details: Trump Media & Technology Group is reportedly offering a premium "Truth API" service for up to $100,000 per month, providing trading firms with early access to high-profile Truth Social posts, including President Trump's potentially market-moving announcements on economic policy and global affairs. This offering has drawn sharp criticism from Democratic senators and securities experts, who argue it could constitute an "outrageous abuse" of office, undermine market integrity, and potentially violate insider trading laws by giving institutional investors an unfair advantage.
title: Trump's Truth Social "Truth API" Raises Ethical Concerns
